description: IPOP-CMA-ES minimises a function of real variables by running CMA-ES many times. Each run starts from a new random mean in the search box. When a run stops by itself, for example because it has converged or stagnated, the next run uses a population that is `factor` times larger (by default two times). A larger population searches more globally, so the restarts help on functions with many local minima (*multimodal* functions). The method has no optimality guarantee: it returns the best point found when the evaluation budget or the restart limit ends it.

papers.title: A Restart CMA Evolution Strategy With Increasing Population Size

lineage.source: evolutionary-planning, src/cmaes.rs: "IPOP-CMA-ES (Auger and Hansen 2005): independent restarts with the population size multiplied by `factor` each time"
